Board service information.

Serving on your condominium or HOA board is a valuable way to contribute to your community. Board members make important decisions about the property's management, finances, and future direction while working with professional management.

Board member responsibilities.

  • Attend regular board meetings, typically monthly
  • Review financial reports and budgets
  • Make decisions on maintenance and improvements
  • Address owner concerns and communications
  • Oversee compliance with the governing documents
  • Work with the property management company

Election process.

Board positions are typically decided by the votes received at the annual election. All eligible unit owners may vote, and in many associations voting power is based on percentage of ownership. The nominating committee reviews applications and may interview candidates before presenting them to the owners for election. Your bylaws and the election notice set who may serve, how many seats are open, and the deadline for nominations.

Learn more about Illinois board elections, proxies, and ballots and how to prepare for the annual meeting.

Common questions.

When is the nomination deadline?

It is set by your bylaws and stated in the election notice. If you do not have the notice, call or email our office and we will tell you.

Do I need to be an owner to serve?

In most associations directors must be unit owners, and some bylaws add requirements such as being current on assessments. Renters can serve only if your bylaws allow it.

Can I nominate another owner?

Yes. Confirm first that they are willing to serve, then ask them to complete this application themselves so the committee has their own answers and signature.

Will my application appear on the ballot?

Eligible applications received before the deadline are included in the election process your bylaws describe. Some associations also accept nominations from the floor at the meeting.
